docs.title: KeyForge Engineering Doctrine: LLM-Integrated Development (LID)
docs.text: Version: 2.2 (Complete) Date: 2025-12-29 Context: Operational protocols for engineering high-reliability distributed systems with Large Language Models.

docs.title: 1. Core Philosophy: Constraint-Based Engineering
docs.text:
LLMs are probabilistic engines, not rational agents. They suffer from Semantic Blindness (confusing syntax with logic), Context Saturation (degrading reasoning as sessions grow), and Happy Path Bias.

To build world-class software, we move from Asking (hoping the LLM is smart) to Constraining (making it impossible for the LLM to be wrong).

"You cannot test quality into a product. Correctness must be a property of the system."

docs.title: The Criticality Tiers
docs.text:
1. Tier 1 (The Nucleus): keyforge-physics, keyforge-evolution.
  2. Role: Pure Logic. Deterministic. Zero IO.
  3. Risk: Mathematical hallucination, silent optimization failure.

  4. Requirement: 95%+ Branch Coverage + Property Testing (proptest) + Shadow Execution.

  5. Tier 2 (The Contract): keyforge-protocol, keyforge-model.

  6. Role: Data Definitions. Validators.
  7. Risk: Data corruption, serialization bombs.

  8. Requirement: 100% Validation Coverage. Use TryFrom to make invalid states unrepresentable.

  9. Tier 3 (The Shell): keyforge-infra, keyforge-hive, keyforge-agent.

  10. Role: IO, Network, Database, State.
  11. Risk: Deadlocks, "Whac-A-Mole" debugging.
  12. Requirement: Error-First Design. Define failure modes (thiserror) before logic.

docs.title: 2. Structural Patterns (The Architecture)
docs.text: We enforce a strict separation of concerns to isolate LLM hallucinations.

docs.title: A. Functional Core, Imperative Shell
docs.text:
We isolate pure logic from the messy real world.

  • The Core (physics, evolution): Pure functions only. Input -> Output. No std::fs, no tokio, no sqlx.
  • Why: If the Core fails, it is a logic bug (reproducible).
  • The Shell (infra, hive): Handles Files, Network, Time, and Database.
  • Why: If the Shell fails, it is an environment issue.
  • Constraint: The Core NEVER imports the Shell.

docs.title: B. The Semantic Firewall (Aggressive Newtyping)
docs.text:
LLMs struggle to track variable meaning across long contexts. We use the compiler to enforce semantics.

  • Rule: Never use primitives (usize, f32) for domain logic signatures.

  • Pattern:

    pub struct KeyIndex(usize);
pub struct CharCode(u16);
// Compiler Error: KeyIndex + CharCode

  • Effect: If Gemini hallucinates and swaps arguments, the code fails to compile immediately.

docs.title: C. Context Compression (The Header Strategy)
docs.text:
Pasting 50k lines of code guarantees hallucination.

  • Strategy: Feed Gemini "Rust Headers" for dependencies.
  • Action: When working on physics, provide only the struct and fn signatures of model and protocol. Strip bodies.
  • Benefit: Reduces token load by ~90%, keeping the attention mechanism focused on the active task.

docs.title: A. Coverage-Driven Verification (CDV)
docs.text:
We use coverage tools (tarpaulin) to identify Logic Dark Matter—code branches generated by the LLM that have never been executed.

  • Rule: High coverage is not a vanity metric; it is a map of "Unknown Territory."
  • Action: If a branch is uncovered, the LLM must write a specific test case to hit it, or the code must be deleted.

docs.title: B. Shadow Execution (The Oracle)
docs.text:
We maintain a "Simple, Slow, Correct" reference implementation alongside the "Fast, Complex" optimized version.

  • Artifact: DeterministicScorer (in verification.rs).
  • Protocol: Every optimization run in debug mode compares ScoringEngine (Fast) vs DeterministicScorer (Slow).
  • Invariant: abs(Fast - Slow) < EPSILON. If this fails, the system panics.

docs.title: C. The "Ghost Code" Strategy
docs.text:
Complex logic overwhelms the LLM's working memory. We provide simplified models for reasoning.

  • Artifact: src/ghost.rs (in Tier 1 crates).
  • Usage: A simplified, pure-Rust model of the complex kernel.
  • Protocol: Force Gemini to implement logic against the Ghost model first. Once the algorithm is proven, translate it to the optimized kernel.

docs.title: 4. The Interaction Protocol (The Process)
docs.text: We use Least-to-Most (LtM) prompting to force "System 2" reasoning.

docs.title: Phase 1: The Contract (No Code)
docs.text:
Prompt:

"We are implementing [Feature].

  1. Define Types: Create Newtypes for inputs/outputs.
  2. Define Invariants: What must never happen? (e.g., 'Index out of bounds').
  3. Draft Tests: Write a proptest that breaks a naive implementation. STOP. Do not write the function body."

docs.title: Phase 2: The Plan (Pseudo-Code)
docs.text:
Prompt:

"Write the logic in Pseudo-Rust. Focus on data flow and borrow lifetimes. Mark unsafe blocks explicitly."

docs.title: Phase 3: The Implementation (Translation)
docs.text:
Prompt:

"Translate the Pseudo-Rust into real Rust using the Types from Phase 1. Ensure it passes the Draft Tests."

docs.title: 5. The Debugging Protocol (Stopping the Spiral)
docs.text: When the compiler screams, Gemini panics and starts "driving the compiler" (random patching).

docs.title: A. The "Reasoning Injection" Loop
docs.text:
Never just paste an error.

Prompt:

"The compiler error is: [Paste ONE error].

  1. Analyze: Explain why this conflicts with the Rust memory model.
  2. Hypothesize: Is this a logic error or a signature mismatch?
  3. Plan: Propose a fix without changing public signatures."

docs.title: B. The "3-Turn Hard Stop"
docs.text:
If Gemini fails to fix a bug after two attempts:

  1. STOP. Do not paste the third error.
  2. REVERT. Undo the last AI change.
  3. RESET. Trigger the "Soft Reset" (below).

docs.title: C. The "Soft Reset"
docs.text:
To clear "bad reasoning" from the context window without reloading files:

Prompt:

"🛑 STOP. IGNORE ALL PREVIOUS ATTEMPTS AT FIXING THIS FUNCTION. We are resetting the approach for [Function Name].

Current Truth:

  1. The clean file content is: [Paste CLEAN code]
  2. The specific error is: [Paste ONE error]

Instruction: Analyze the error against the clean code. Explain the fix in one sentence, then generate the code."

docs.title: KeyForge Code Review Checklist
docs.text: Context: Mandatory checks before merging LLM-generated code.

docs.title: 1. The Comprehension Test (Human Layer)
docs.text:
• [ ] Explainability: Can I explain this logic to a junior engineer without reading the PR description?
  • [ ] No Magic: Are macros, complex generics, or unsafe blocks used? (Reject if yes, unless justified).
  • [ ] Naming: Do variable names reflect Domain Concepts (e.g., finger_load) or Implementation Details (e.g., f32_val)?

docs.title: 2. The Reliability Test (Machine Layer)
docs.text:
• [ ] Coverage: Did cargo tarpaulin confirm 95%+ coverage on new logic?
  • [ ] Mutation: Did cargo mutants pass (no surviving mutants)?
  • [ ] Shadow Execution: Is the DeterministicScorer updated to match any changes in ScoringEngine?

docs.title: 3. The Hallucination Check (AI Layer)
docs.text:
• [ ] Argument Swapping: Check all function calls with multiple arguments of the same type (usize, f32).
  • [ ] Temporal Coupling: Does the code assume a state (e.g., "Job is running") without checking it?
  • [ ] Happy Path Bias: Are error cases (Disk full, Network down, Invalid UTF-8) handled explicitly?

docs.title: 4. The Database Safety Check
docs.text:
• [ ] Zero-Touch: Was the migration generated by a tool/human, NOT the LLM?
  • [ ] Additive Only: Does the migration only add columns/tables? (No DROP).

docs.title: 5. The "Soft Reset" Trigger
docs.text: • [ ] If the PR required > 3 attempts to fix a bug, REJECT. Request a "Soft Reset" and fresh implementation.

docs.title: KeyForge Engineering Manifesto (v6.0)
docs.text: Goal: Engineering Truth, Deterministic State, & Operational Efficiency. Enemy: Context Saturation, Implicit Logic, "Happy Path" Bias. Doctrine: LLM-Integrated Development (LID).

docs.title: 1. Core Philosophy: Constraint-Based Engineering
docs.text: We move from Asking (hoping the LLM is smart) to Constraining (making it impossible for the LLM to be wrong).

docs.title: Criticality Tiering
docs.text:
1. Tier 1 (The Nucleus): keyforge-physics, keyforge-evolution.
  2. Risk: Mathematical hallucination.

  3. Requirement: 95%+ Branch Coverage + Property Testing.

  4. Tier 2 (The Contract): keyforge-protocol, keyforge-model.

  5. Risk: Data corruption.

  6. Requirement: 100% Validation Coverage.

  7. Tier 3 (The Shell): keyforge-infra, keyforge-hive.

  8. Risk: IO/State failure.
  9. Requirement: Error Path Verification.

docs.title: A. The Semantic Firewall (Type-Driven Design)
docs.text:
1. The Typestate Pattern (Compiler State Machine)
  2. Problem: Temporal Coupling (LLM accesses data before it is ready).
  3. Fix: Encode state in types (PendingJob -> RunningJob -> CompletedJob).

  4. Rationale: The compiler prevents accessing score on a PendingJob.

  5. The Parameter Object (Context Structs)

  6. Problem: Argument Swapping (LLM confuses usize arguments).
  7. Fix: Group cohesive arguments into a Context Struct (ScoringContext { layout, corpus }).

  8. Rationale: Fields are named; positional arguments are eliminated.

  9. The Centralized Error Registry

  10. Problem: Lazy error handling (anyhow!, unwrap()).
  11. Fix: A strict, enumerated catalog (ForgeError) in keyforge-protocol.
  12. Rationale: Forces the LLM to categorize failure modes (Physics vs Infra).

docs.title: B. Structural Patterns (Isolation)
docs.text:
1. The Command Pattern (Reified Actions)
  2. Problem: Logic coupled to HTTP Handlers is hard to test.
  3. Fix: Decouple Intent (HiveCommand) from Execution (handle_command).

  4. Rationale: Enables testing business logic without spinning up a server.

  5. The Humble Object

  6. Rule: Extract logic from IO boundaries into pure structs.

  7. Vertical Slices

  8. Rule: Group code by Feature (src/features/register_job), not Layer.

  9. Railway Oriented Programming (ROP)

  10. Rule: Linear Result chains. No nested if/else.

docs.title: A. The Oracle Pattern (Shadow Execution)
docs.text:
• Rule: ScoringEngine (Optimized) must match DeterministicScorer (Simple) bit-for-bit.
  • Protocol: Run both in Debug builds. Panic on divergence.

docs.title: B. Coverage-Driven Verification (CDV)
docs.text:
• Goal: Identify "Logic Dark Matter" (unexecuted branches).
  • Rule: High coverage is a map of "Unknown Territory".

docs.title: C. Advanced Testing Protocols
docs.text:
1. Mutation Testing (cargo-mutants): Zero "Survived Mutants" allowed in Physics.
  2. Metamorphic Testing: Verify properties (dist(a,b) == dist(b,a)).
  3. Golden Data: Use hardcoded input/output pairs (tests/fixtures/) as the Anchor of Truth.
  4. Formal Verification Lite (kani): Prove invariants for core math.
  5. Snapshot Testing (insta): Lock regression for complex DTOs/Parsers.

docs.title: D. The Ghost Code Strategy
docs.text: • Rule: For complex algorithms, implement a simplified "Ghost Model" first. Prove it, then optimize.

docs.title: A. The SAGA Loop
docs.text:
1. Isolation: Debug in repro.rs.
  2. Tests First: Test -> Fail -> Implement -> Pass.
  3. Signature Freeze: No changing pub signatures during debugging.
  4. 3-Turn Stop: If fix fails twice: STOP, REVERT, ISOLATE.

docs.title: B. Context Management
docs.text:
1. The Cleanroom: Never debug inside the full app context.
  2. Context Compression: Use "Header Files" (Signatures only) for dependencies.
  3. The Soft Reset: Clear context window if reasoning degrades.

docs.title: C. The Reflexion Loop
docs.text:
• Protocol: When a test fails:
    1. Input: Failing Test + Code.
    2. Task: "Explain the logic error in natural language."
    3. Action: Generate fix based on explanation.

docs.title: D. Chain-of-Verification (CoVe)
docs.text: • Protocol: Draft -> Verify (Manual Calc) -> Finalize.

docs.title: A. Database Safety
docs.text:
• Rule: Zero-Touch Migrations.
  • Protocol: Never write SQL migrations directly. Output schema, verify diff. Migrations must be Additive Only.

docs.title: B. Human Protocols
docs.text:
1. The Comprehension Test: Human must explain logic without reading LLM summary.
  2. The Two-Man Audit: Coder != Auditor. Use fresh context for security audit.
  3. No Magic: Reject macros/complex generics unless explicitly requested.

docs.title: C. Tiered Verification (CI Economics)
docs.text:
1. Tier 1: The Fast Loop (Local): cargo check, cargo test (Unit). Time: < 30s.
  2. Tier 2: The Logic Loop (PR): cargo test --doc, cargo mutants (Diff). Time: < 10m.
  3. Tier 3: The Deep Freeze (Nightly): kani, Full cargo mutants, E2E. Time: Hours.

docs.title: Domain Dictionary (Ubiquitous Language)
docs.text:
Version: 4.1 Status: Active Source: libs/keyforge-model/src/lib.rs

This document defines the strict terminology used throughout the KeyForge codebase.

docs.title: 1. Physical Domain (The Hardware)
docs.text: Term Type Definition Validation Rule Keyboard Keyboard The immutable physical definition. Contains Vec<KeyNode> and geometry data. Must have >0 keys. KeyNode KeyNode A single physical key. Properties: index, finger, hand, x, y, row, col. Dimensions > 0. Valid Hand/Finger. KeyIndex KeyIndex(usize) Canonical index (0..N) of a physical key. Invariant: Stable for a specific hardware definition. 0 <= index < key_count. Hand HandIndex(u8) Left (0) or Right (1). Used for balance and split-keyboard logic. Must be 0 or 1. Finger FingerIndex(u8) Thumbs (0), Index (1), Middle (2), Ring (3), Pinky (4). Must be 0..=4.

docs.title: 2. Logical Domain (The Mapping)
docs.text: Term Type Definition Validation Rule Layout Layout A mapping of KeyCodes to KeyIndexes. The mutable entity evolved by the optimizer. No duplicate keys. Length matches Keyboard. KeyCode KeyCode(u16) A logical character or action. Decoupled from physical position. ID/Label cannot be empty. Pinned Keys Vec<Option<KeyCode>> A mask of keys that the optimizer is forbidden from moving (e.g., Spacebar, Enter). Indices must be in bounds.

docs.title: 3. Analysis Domain (The Physics)
docs.text: Term Type Definition Validation Rule Corpus Corpus Source text data. Contains N-gram frequencies (Bigrams, Trigrams). char_freqs len == 65536. Rubric Rubric Configuration defining how to score. Weights for sfb, distance, roll, etc. Weights must be finite & positive. Score f32 The calculated "Cost" of a layout. Lower is Better. Must be finite. AnalysisReport AnalysisReport Detailed breakdown including sfb_ratio, heatmap, hand_balance, and top_sfbs. N/A (Output).

docs.title: 4. Optimization Domain (The Evolution)
docs.text: Term Type Definition Validation Rule SearchConfig SearchConfig Configuration for the Simulated Annealing loop (Temperature, Steps, Patience). steps > 0, temp_min < temp_max. OptimizationResult OptimizationResult The final output tuple: { score: f32, layout: Layout }. N/A (Output).

docs.title: Entity Relationship Models
docs.text: Version: 4.0 Context: keyforge-model and keyforge-physics Aggregates.

docs.title: 1. The Optimization Aggregate
docs.text:
The EngineRequest is the root aggregate that defines a "Job". It is composed of immutable reference data (Arc) and mutable configuration.

classDiagram
    class EngineRequest {
        +Arc~Keyboard~ keyboard
        +Arc~Corpus~ corpus
        +Arc~Rubric~ rubric
        +SearchConfig config
        +Option~Layout~ initial_layout
        +Vec~Option~KeyCode~~ pinned_keys
    }

    class Keyboard {
        +Vec~KeyNode~ keys
        +usize key_count
    }

    class KeyNode {
        +KeyIndex index
        +FingerIndex finger
        +HandIndex hand
        +f32 x
        +f32 y
    }

    class Corpus {
        +Vec~u64~ char_freqs
        +Vec~Bigram~ bigrams
        +Vec~Trigram~ trigrams
    }

    class Rubric {
        +f32 sfb_weight
        +f32 distance_weight
        +f32 roll_weight
    }

    class Layout {
        +Vec~KeyCode~ keys
    }

    EngineRequest *-- Keyboard : Shared (Arc)
    EngineRequest *-- Corpus : Shared (Arc)
    EngineRequest *-- Rubric : Shared (Arc)
    EngineRequest *-- Layout : Owns (Optional)
    Keyboard *-- KeyNode : Contains

docs.title: 2. The Scoring Engine (Compiler Pattern)
docs.text:
The ScoringEngine compiles the raw data into an optimized EngineContext for high-performance scoring.

classDiagram
    class ScoringEngine {
        +score(Layout) f32
        +analyze(Layout) AnalysisReport
    }

    class EngineContext {
        +usize key_count
        +Vec~f32~ cost_matrix
        +LookupTables tables
    }

    class Compiler {
        +compile(Keyboard, Corpus, Rubric) EngineContext
    }

    ScoringEngine *-- EngineContext : Owns
    Compiler ..> EngineContext : Creates
    Compiler ..> Keyboard : Reads
    Compiler ..> Corpus : Reads

docs.title: 3. The Evolution Loop
docs.text:
The Optimizer orchestrates the mutation of the Layout using the ScoringEngine as an oracle.

sequenceDiagram
    participant Supervisor as Optimizer
    participant Engine as ScoringEngine
    participant Layout as Layout

    Supervisor->>Engine: new(Request)
    Engine-->>Supervisor: Ready

    loop Annealing Steps
        Supervisor->>Layout: Mutate (Swap Keys)
        Supervisor->>Engine: score(Layout)
        Engine-->>Supervisor: Score (Cost)

        alt Score Improved OR Temperature Check
            Supervisor->>Supervisor: Accept New Layout
        else
            Supervisor->>Layout: Revert Swap
        end

        opt Every N Steps
            Supervisor->>User: ProgressCallback
        end
    end

    Supervisor->>User: OptimizationResult

docs.text:
What happens when a worker pulls a job but dies before finishing?

sequenceDiagram
    participant Monitor as Hive::Monitor
    participant DB
    participant Queue

    loop Every 60s
        Monitor->>DB: Scan for Stale Jobs
        Note right of Monitor: "Running" > 5 mins ago<br/>AND No Heartbeat

        DB-->>Monitor: List[Job 123]

        Monitor->>DB: Increment Retry Count

            Monitor->>DB: Set Status = Pending

            Monitor->>DB: Set Status = Failed

docs.title: Design Patterns & Architectural Styles
docs.text: Version: 4.3 Context: Key patterns used to enforce reliability and maintainability.

docs.title: 1. The Typestate Pattern (Compiler State Machine)
docs.text:
Target: keyforge-hive, keyforge-agent

We use the Type System to prevent invalid state transitions. Instead of a single struct with a status enum, we use distinct types.

  • Bad: struct Job { status: String, result: Option<f32> }
  • Good:
  • struct PendingJob { config: Config }
  • struct RunningJob { start_time: Instant }
  • struct CompletedJob { score: f32 }

Benefit: It is impossible to access the score of a pending job.

docs.title: 2. The Parameter Object (Context Structs)
docs.text:
Target: keyforge-physics

To prevent "Argument Swapping" in functions with many parameters of the same type (f32, usize), we group cohesive arguments into Context Structs.

pub struct ScoringContext<'a> {
    pub layout: &'a Layout,
    pub corpus: &'a Corpus,
    pub rubric: &'a Rubric,
}

// Signature: fn score(ctx: ScoringContext) -> Score

docs.title: 3. The Command Pattern (Reified Actions)
docs.text:
Target: keyforge-hive

We decouple the "Intent" (Command) from the "Execution" (Handler). This allows logic to be tested without an HTTP server.

pub enum HiveCommand {
    RegisterJob(JobRequest),
    CancelJob(String),
}

docs.title: 4. The Centralized Error Registry
docs.text:
Target: keyforge-protocol

We forbid lazy error handling (anyhow). All errors must be enumerated in a central registry to ensure clients can handle them programmatically.

#[derive(Error, Debug)]
pub enum ForgeError {
    #[error("Physics Violation: Score {0} is negative")]
    PhysicsViolation(f32),
    #[error("Stale Job: {0}")]
    StaleJob(String),
}

docs.title: 5. Vertical Slice Architecture
docs.text:
Target: apps/keyforge-hive

Organize code by Feature, not by technical layer.

  • src/features/register_job/ (Contains Handler, Logic, Models)
  • src/features/get_results/

docs.title: 6. The Humble Object Pattern
docs.text:
Target: IO Boundaries

Strip logic out of the "Driver" (HTTP Handler, CLI Command) and move it to a pure, testable function.

docs.title: 7. The Hybrid DTO Pattern
docs.text:
Target: keyforge-protocol / keyforge-model

To avoid the boilerplate of maintaining duplicate structs (e.g., JobRequestDto vs JobRequestDomain), we embed Domain Entities directly inside Data Transfer Objects.

  • The DTO (JobRequest): Acts as the "Envelope". It handles serialization and Protocol-level validation (Versioning, Request Limits).
  • The Domain Entity (KeyboardDefinition): Acts as the "Payload". It handles Business Logic validation (Physics, Geometry).

The Validation Chain: The DTO implements Validator and must delegate validation to its embedded Domain Entities.

impl Validator for JobRequest {
    fn validate(&self) -> Result<(), String> {
        // 1. Protocol Check (The Bouncer)
        if self.biometrics.len() > 1000 { return Err("Too big"); }

        // 2. Domain Check (The Rules)
        self.definition.validate()?; 

        Ok(())
    }
}

docs.title: 8. The Agent Runner Pattern
docs.text:
Target: keyforge-cli

Decouples User Intent (CLI Arguments) from Execution (Physics). The CLI acts as a Manager that prepares the environment and configuration, then spawns the Worker to do the job.

  • Mechanism: CLI builds JobConfig -> Serializes to JSON -> Spawns keyforge-agent run job.json -> Streams stdout to User.
  • Benefit: Ensures that "Local Search" and "Remote Job" run on identical physics engines.

docs.title: Failure Mode Analysis (FMA)
docs.text: Version: 4.1 Context: Known failure states and recovery strategies.

docs.title: 1. Infrastructure Failures
docs.text: Component Failure Mode Detection Recovery Strategy Database Connection Lost InfraError::DbConnection Retry (Exponential Backoff). If exhausted, return 503 Service Unavailable. Coordination Valkey Unreachable InfraError::Io Degrade. Real-time stats freeze. Write-shield fails open (assume new profile). FileSystem Disk Full InfraError::Io Crash. Alert Admin. No automatic recovery possible. Network Upstream Timeout InfraError::Network Retry (3 attempts). If failed, serve stale cache if available, else Error.

docs.title: 2. Application Failures
docs.text: Component Failure Mode Detection Recovery Strategy Worker Node Crash / Timeout Heartbeat Missed Re-queue. The Job is returned to the queue for another worker to pick up. Physics Panic (e.g., Div by 0) std::panic::catch_unwind Isolate. The specific optimization run fails, but the Worker process survives. Report error to Hive. Job Poison Pill (Invalid Config) Validation Error Reject. Mark Job as Failed in DB. Do not re-queue.

docs.title: 3. Logic Failures
docs.text: Component Failure Mode Detection Recovery Strategy Scoring Score Overflow Score Type Bounds Saturate. Cap at Score::MAX. Log warning. Evolution Stagnation (Local Minima) patience counter Reheat. Increase temperature to escape. If failed, terminate early.

docs.text: Version: 4.0 Context: Authentication, Authorization, and Threat Mitigation.

docs.text:
• Trusted Zone: keyforge-hive (Server), keyforge-infra (Database).

  • Untrusted: Public Internet, User Submissions.

docs.text:

  • Client sends Authorization: Bearer <SECRET>.
  • Middleware (auth::require_secret) validates hash.

docs.text:
Implemented via governor (Token Bucket).

Tier Limit Burst Target Global 1000 req/s 2000 All IPs. Protects against volumetric attacks. Strict 1 req/s 5 Expensive endpoints (POST /jobs, POST /results).

docs.title: ADR-001: Hexagonal Architecture
docs.text:
• Status: Accepted
  • Date: 2024-01-01
  • Context: We need to swap databases and frontends without rewriting core logic.
  • Decision: Use Ports & Adapters. keyforge-physics must have ZERO dependencies on keyforge-infra.
  • Consequences:
  • (+) Core logic is purely testable.
  • (-) Boilerplate for DTO conversion.

docs.title: ADR-002: No Async in Physics
docs.text:
• Status: Accepted
  • Date: 2024-01-15
  • Context: Scoring is CPU-bound. Async overhead slows down tight loops.
  • Decision: keyforge-physics and keyforge-evolution will be synchronous.
  • Consequences:
  • (+) Maximum CPU throughput.
  • (-) Workers must use spawn_blocking to prevent blocking the reactor.

docs.title: ADR-003: Shared Secret Auth
docs.text:
• Status: Accepted
  • Date: 2024-02-01
  • Context: We need a simple way to secure a private cluster. OAuth is overkill.
  • Decision: Use a static Shared Secret (Bearer Token).
  • Consequences:
  • (+) Simple to implement.
  • (-) Key rotation requires restarting all nodes.

docs.title: ADR-004: Postcard for Deterministic Hashing
docs.text:
• Status: Accepted
  • Date: 2025-12-30
  • Context: bincode is unmaintained. We need a stable, deterministic binary serialization format for generating JobIdentifier hashes.
  • Decision: Replace bincode with postcard.
  • Consequences:
  • (+) Maintained, no_std compatible, designed for embedded/deterministic use.
  • (-) Breaking change for existing Job IDs (hashes will change).

docs.title: ADR-005: Feature Gating TypeScript Bindings
docs.text:
• Status: Accepted
  • Date: 2025-12-30
  • Context: ts-rs emits warnings about #[serde] attributes it doesn't understand (like deserialize_with). These warnings pollute the build log.
  • Decision: Gate ts-rs behind a ts_bindings feature flag.
  • Consequences:
  • (+) Clean build logs for standard development (cargo test).
  • (+) Reduced dependency footprint for production builds.
  • (-) Developers must explicitly run cargo test --features ts_bindings to verify bindings.

docs.title: ADR-006: Universal Domain Validation
docs.text:
• Status: Accepted
  • Date: 2025-12-31
  • Context: Domain entities were being deserialized at various boundaries (API, Disk, WASM) without consistent validation.
  • Decision: Implement the Validator trait for all Domain Entities in keyforge-model. Enforce .validate() calls immediately after deserialization at all system boundaries.
  • Consequences:
  • (+) Guarantees invalid data is caught at the IO boundary before entering the domain.
  • (+) Centralizes validation logic in the Model layer.
  • (-) Requires boilerplate Validator implementations for simple structs.

docs.title: ADR-007: Lowercase Alpha Normalization
docs.text:
• Status: Accepted
  • Date: 2025-12-31
  • Context: Keyboards send keycodes (e.g., KC_A), but text corpora usually contain lowercase characters ('a').
  • Decision: Normalize all alphabetic keycodes to lowercase internally within the Domain Model. Uppercase is treated purely as a Presentation Layer concern.
  • Consequences:
  • (+) Simplifies scoring logic.
  • (+) Consistent with standard text corpora.
  • (-) UI must explicitly uppercase keys for display if desired.

docs.title: ADR-008: Synthetic Corpus Injection
docs.text:
• Status: Accepted
  • Date: 2026-01-02
  • Context: Standard text corpora lack explicit Enter and Backspace events, leading to suboptimal placement of these keys.
  • Decision: Inject synthetic frequency data for Enter and Backspace into _std corpora at load time based on error rate and punctuation models.
  • Consequences:
  • (+) Layouts optimize for realistic typing flows, including errors and formatting.
  • (+) Backspace and Enter are pulled closer to the home row.
  • (-) Synthetic distribution is heuristic.

docs.title: ADR-009: Optimal Choice for Duplicate Keys
docs.text:
• Status: Accepted
  • Date: 2026-01-06
  • Context: Keyboards often feature duplicate keys (e.g., split spacebars or bilateral modifiers). Previous logic used a "last one wins" or "distributed load" approach, which failed to model an "optimal typist" who chooses the best physical key for a given context.
  • Decision: Implement "Optimal Choice" logic. For every monogram, bigram, and trigram, the engine dynamically searches all physical instances of the involved characters to find the specific key (or combination) that yields the absolute minimum cost.
  • Consequences:
  • (+) More realistic modeling of advanced and split layouts.
  • (+) Provides the architectural foundation for future stateful keys (e.g., Repeat key).
  • (+) Simplifies physics by removing SpaceHandPreference (now handled by the typist model).
  • (-) Increased computational complexity in the fast-path score_layout due to dynamic searching.

docs.title: ADR-010: Distributed Coordination via Valkey
docs.text:
• Status: Accepted
  • Date: 2026-01-07
  • Context:
  • Process Isolation: The Hive WebSocket event loop was process-local (tokio::broadcast). If we scaled Hive to multiple instances, users connected to Instance A could not see events from Instance B.
  • Database Load: High-frequency ephemeral data (Agent Heartbeats at 1Hz, Real-time Score updates) was being written to PostgreSQL, causing write amplification and WAL bloat for data that has no long-term value.oo
  • Consistency: Asset caches were managed locally. If an admin updated a file on one server, others would serve stale data.
  • Decision: Introduce Valkey (an open-source Redis fork) as the Coordination Layer.
  • Role: Acts as the "Nervous System" for the cluster.
  • Mechanism:
    • Heartbeats: SETEX keys with TTL (Auto-expiry for dead nodes).
    • Chatter: PUBLISH/SUBSCRIBE for real-time score updates across the cluster.
    • Manifest: Stores the authoritative hash of system assets to ensure consistency.
  • Consequences:
  • (+) Scalability: Hive is now stateless and can scale horizontally.
  • (+) Observability: Real-time visibility into Agent temperature/IPS without SQL polling.
  • (+) Efficiency: Zero SQL writes for ephemeral state.
  • (-) Complexity: Adds a 4th container to the stack.
  • (-) Dependency: Hive requires Valkey to start (hard dependency for coordination).
  • (-) Refactor: Requires testcontainers for integration testing.

docs.title: ADR-011: The Thin Client CLI (Agent Runner)
docs.text:
• Status: Accepted
  • Date: 2026-01-10
  • Context: The CLI previously statically linked keyforge-compute and keyforge-physics. This created two execution environments: Local (CLI-embedded engine) and Remote (Agent-embedded engine). Ensuring parity was difficult and CLI compile times were slow.
  • Decision: Refactor the CLI into a "Thin Client". It performs IO and Asset Management but delegates all heavy lifting (search, bench, validate) to the keyforge-agent binary via subprocess spawning.
  • Consequences:
  • (+) Parity: Local and Remote runs use the exact same binary (keyforge-agent).
  • (+) Build Times: CLI compiles faster as it drops heavy math dependencies.
  • (-) UX: Requires user to have keyforge-agent in PATH or side-loaded.

docs.title: ADR-012: The Control/Asset Plane Split
docs.text:
• Status: Accepted
  • Date: 2026-01-12
  • Context: Hive currently handles both "Logic" (Jobs, Auth) and "Content" (Serving 50MB corpus files). High download traffic from agents/CLIs competes with the API's CPU resources.
  • Decision: Split the architecture into two distinct services:
  • Hive (Control Plane): Handles orchestration, auth, and state.
  • Assets (Data Plane): A dedicated, stateless HTTP service that streams assets directly from Valkey.
  • Consequences:
  • (+) Scalability: Asset Server can be cached via CDN or scaled independently.
  • (+) Security: Asset Server can be public (read-only), while Hive remains private/authenticated.
  • (+) Architecture: Explicit separation of concerns.
  • (-) Complexity: Clients must manage two base URLs (KEYFORGE_API_URL and KEYFORGE_ASSET_URL).

docs.title: State Models & Lifecycles
docs.text: Version: 4.0 Context: Finite State Machines (FSM) governing system behavior.

docs.title: 1. The Optimization Loop (Annealing)
docs.text:
This process runs inside keyforge-evolution. It is synchronous and CPU-bound.

stateDiagram-v2
    [*] --> Init : optimize(Request)

    state Init {
        [*] --> Validate : Check Config
        Validate --> Compile : Build ScoringEngine
        Compile --> Pin : Apply Pinned Keys
    }

    Init --> Annealing : Engine Ready

    state Annealing {
        [*] --> Mutate : GroupMutation
        Mutate --> Score : Engine.score()
        Score --> Evaluate : Calculate Delta

        Evaluate --> Accept : Delta < 0 (Better)
        Evaluate --> Probabilistic : Delta > 0 (Worse)

        Probabilistic --> Accept : Random < Temp
        Probabilistic --> Reject : Random > Temp

        Accept --> UpdateBest : If Score < GlobalBest
        Reject --> Revert : Undo Swap

        UpdateBest --> Cool : Temp * Decay
        Revert --> Cool

        Cool --> CheckPatience

        state CheckPatience {
            [*] --> Continue : Patience > 0
            Continue --> [*]

            [*] --> Reheat : Patience == 0
            Reheat --> Continue : Reheats Remaining
            Reheat --> Terminate : No Reheats Left
        }
    }

    Annealing --> Result : Terminate or Max Steps
    Result --> [*]

docs.title: 2. The Worker Job Lifecycle
docs.text:
The lifecycle of a Job as it moves through the distributed system.

stateDiagram-v2
    [*] --> Pending : Submitted via API

    Pending --> Assigned : Worker Polling
    Assigned --> Running : Worker Accepted

    state Running {
        [*] --> Downloading : Fetch Assets
        Downloading --> Optimizing : Evolution Loop
        Optimizing --> Signing : Sign Result (Ed25519)
    }

    Running --> Completed : Result Validated
    Running --> Failed : Panic / Timeout

    Completed --> [*]
    Failed --> Pending : Retry < 3
    Failed --> DeadLetter : Retry >= 3

For real-time cluster management without a web browser, we provide a Terminal User Interface.

  • Tool: ratatui (Rust).
  • Binary: keyforge-admin.
  • Connectivity: Connects via SSH tunnel or local socket to the Hive API.

docs.title: Configuration Schema
docs.text: Version: 4.0 Context: Tunable parameters for the Physics and Evolution engines.

docs.title: 1. SearchConfig (Simulated Annealing)
docs.text:
The SearchConfig struct controls the behavior of the optimizer.

Parameter Type Default Description Constraints steps usize 100,000 The maximum number of mutations to attempt. Must be > 0. start_temp f32 100.0 Initial temperature. Higher values allow more chaotic jumps early on. Must be >= 0. end_temp f32 0.01 Final temperature target. Determines the decay rate. Must be >= 0. seed u64 42 The PRNG seed. Ensures deterministic runs for debugging. None. patience usize 500 Number of steps without improvement before triggering a Reheat. Must be > 0. reheats usize 3 How many times to spike the temperature back up if stuck in a local minimum. Must be >= 0. reheat_factor f32 0.5 Multiplier for start_temp when reheating (e.g., 0.5 * 100.0 = 50.0). Must be > 0.

docs.title: 2. Rubric (Scoring Weights)
docs.text:
The Rubric defines the "Personality" of the layout (e.g., Comfort vs Speed).

Parameter Type Description sfb_weight f32 Penalty for using the same finger twice in a row. distance_weight f32 Penalty for finger travel distance. roll_weight f32 Bonus (negative cost) for inward rolling motions. redirect_weight f32 Penalty for changing direction mid-stream (e.g., Left -> Right -> Left).

docs.title: Operational Strategy (Day-2 Operations)
docs.text: Version: 4.6 Context: Maintenance, Scaling, Reliability, and Containerization.

docs.title: 1. Database Migrations
docs.text:
• Tool: sqlx-cli.
  • Policy: Zero-downtime migrations.
  • Add columns: Safe.
  • Drop columns: Forbidden until code usage is removed in previous deployment.
  • Execution: The Application Entrypoint runs sqlx::migrate!().run() on startup. If migration fails, the container crashes (CrashLoopBackOff) to prevent data corruption.

docs.title: 2. Distributed Coordination (Valkey)
docs.text: KeyForge uses Valkey (Redis-compatible) as a high-speed coordination layer. It supplies four critical functions that remove load from the primary database:

docs.title: A. The Write Shield (Locking)
docs.text:
• Function: try_reserve_profile_update
  • Role: Prevents "Thundering Herd" attacks on the hardware_profiles SQL table. It acts as a distributed lock/cache, ensuring only one Hive instance attempts to write a specific CPU profile to disk per 24 hours.

docs.title: B. The Heartbeat Aggregator
docs.text:
• Function: update_heartbeat / get_cluster_stats
  • Role: Stores ephemeral node telemetry (IPS, Temperature, RAM) with a 30-second TTL. This removes 99% of UPDATE nodes SET ... traffic from the primary database.

docs.title: C. The Source of Truth for Assets
docs.text:
• Function: set_manifest_entry / get_bin
  • Role: Stores the authoritative SHA-256 hash of system assets and the binary content itself. This decouples file serving from the API logic.

docs.title: D. The Event Bus (Pub/Sub)
docs.text:
• Function: publish_update
  • Role: Broadcasts job status changes (e.g., "Job 123 Completed") to all connected clients instantly, regardless of which server instance they are connected to.

docs.title: 3. The Asset Lifecycle (Data Plane)
docs.text: The Asset Architecture follows a strict Writer/Reader separation.

docs.title: The Manager (keyforge-assetmgr)
docs.text:
• Role: The Write Master (Daemon).
  • Privileges: Read/Write access to Valkey. Read access to Disk.
  • Lifecycle: Long-running process.
  • Behavior:
    1. Boot: Scans data/system, validates every file, and hydrates Valkey.
    2. Runtime: Watches the filesystem using OS-native events (inotify/FSEvents).
    3. Update: When a file changes, it re-validates and re-uploads atomically.
    4. Notify: Publishes asset_update events to the cluster so caches can be invalidated.

docs.title: The Server (keyforge-assets)
docs.text:
• Role: The Read Replica (Gateway).
  • Privileges: Read-Only access to Valkey. No Disk access required.
  • Lifecycle: Stateless request handler.
  • Behavior: Serves HTTP requests by streaming data directly from Valkey memory.

docs.title: 4. Containerization Strategy
docs.text: We adhere to the Minimal Attack Surface doctrine.

docs.title: Rust Services (hive, assets, assetmgr)
docs.text:
• Base Image: gcr.io/distroless/cc-debian12
  • Components: Contains only the compiled binary, glibc, libssl, and libgcc.
  • Security: No shell (/bin/sh), no package manager (apt), no temp files.
  • Size: ~25MB compressed.

docs.title: Infrastructure Services
docs.text:
• Database: postgres:16-alpine. Standard minimal image based on Alpine Linux.
  • Web Proxy: httpd:alpine. Minimal Apache build based on Alpine Linux.

docs.title: 5. Secret Management
docs.text:
• Storage: Environment Variables (HIVE_SECRET, DATABASE_URL, KEYFORGE_VALKEY_URL).
  • Rotation:
  • Update the Secret in the Orchestrator.
  • Trigger a Rolling Restart.
  • Nodes re-authenticate with the new secret.

docs.title: 6. Disaster Recovery
docs.text:
• RPO: 24 Hours (Daily Backups).
  • RTO: 1 Hour (Redeploy Stack).
  • Strategy: Postgres Dump for persistent state. Assets re-hydrated automatically by assetmgr from the mounted volume or container image.

docs.title: Testing Standards & Verification
docs.text: Version: 4.1 Context: Verification methodology, CDV, and Mutation Analysis.

docs.title: 1. The Oracle Pattern
docs.text: To verify the correctness of our highly optimized, bit-twiddling ScoringEngine, we employ a Simple Oracle.

docs.title: The Concept
docs.text:
• Implementation: A naive, readable, inefficient implementation of the logic.
  • Usage: Property Tests generate random inputs and assert Optimized.result() == Oracle.result().

docs.title: Physics Oracle
docs.text:
• Optimized: Uses flattened Vec<f32>, pre-calculated lookups, and unsafe indices (checked at compile time).
  • Oracle: Uses HashMap<(char, char), f32> and standard iteration.
  • Invariant: The score must match exactly (bitwise equality for integers, epsilon for floats).

docs.title: 2. Coverage-Driven Verification (CDV)
docs.text: We use code coverage (tarpaulin) to identify Logic Dark Matter—code branches generated by the LLM that have never been executed.

docs.title: Criticality Tiering
docs.text:
1. Tier 1 (The Nucleus): keyforge-physics, keyforge-evolution.
    • Requirement: 95%+ Branch Coverage + Property Testing.
  2. Tier 2 (The Contract): keyforge-protocol, keyforge-model.
    • Requirement: 100% Validation Coverage.
  3. Tier 3 (The Shell): keyforge-infra, keyforge-hive.
    • Requirement: Error Path Verification.

docs.title: 3. Mutation Testing (cargo-mutants)
docs.text:
We do not just test that the code works; we test that the tests work.

  • Tool: cargo-mutants.
  • Mechanism: The tool injects synthetic bugs (mutants) into the source code (e.g., changing + to -, or if x < y to if x <= y) and runs the test suite.
  • Success: The test suite FAILS (The mutant is "Caught").
  • Failure: The test suite PASSES (The mutant "Survived"). This indicates a gap in test coverage.

Rule: A PR affecting keyforge-physics cannot be merged if it introduces "Survived Mutants".

docs.title: 4. The Reflexion Loop
docs.text:
When a property test or mutation test fails, we enforce a reflection step:

  1. Input: Failing test case + Code.
  2. Task: "Explain the logic error in natural language."
  3. Action: "Generate the fix based on that explanation."

docs.title: 5. Performance Budget
docs.text:
Tier 1 code must adhere to strict latency budgets.

Component Budget (per op) Benchmark ScoringEngine::score < 50ns cargo bench --bench physics Mutation::swap < 5ns cargo bench --bench mutation Anneal Step < 100ns Aggregate of swap + score + decision.

docs.title: Corpora & Data Processing
docs.text: This document details the acquisition, cleansing, and validation strategies for the text corpora used to generate frequency statistics (N-grams and words) for Keyforge.

docs.title: 1. Data Cleansing Philosophy
docs.text: The primary goal of the Keyforge data pipeline is to model standard English typing behavior on a standard ANSI keyboard. The cleansing strategy prioritizes data purity over data recovery.

docs.title: Core Principles
docs.text:
1. Strict Whitelist: Only standard ASCII characters (Decimal 32-126) are permitted. Any character outside this range (e.g., Unicode, Diacritics, Control Codes) is considered "Foreign" or "Noise."
  2. Taint Propagation: If a word buffer contains even a single invalid character (e.g., "café", "naïve", or binary garbage), the entire word is discarded. We do not attempt to "salvage" the valid parts, as this creates partial non-words.
  3. Flow Interruption: When a word is tainted and discarded, the N-gram statistical chain is reset. The preceding word is not stitched to the following word, preventing the generation of phantom bigrams that never occurred in the source text.
  4. Ground Truth Verification: Validity is not determined by heuristics alone but by cross-referencing the output against a standard English dictionary.

docs.title: 2. Corpus: en_std (Modern English Prose)
docs.text: The en_std corpus represents Standard Modern English with a focus on creative writing, dialogue, and narrative flow.

docs.title: 2.1 Source Data
docs.text:
• Dataset Name: lucadiliello/bookcorpusopen (Hugging Face)
  • Description: An open replication of the original BookCorpus dataset.
  • Volume: ~6 Billion characters.
  • Format: Parquet (Columnar).

docs.title: 2.2 Processing Pipeline
docs.text: The raw data undergoes a parallel, zero-copy streaming transformation using a custom Rust tokenizer.

docs.title: Step 1: Normalization
docs.text:
Before validation, specific characters are mapped to their standard ASCII equivalents.

Category Source Character(s) Mapped To Quotes “ ” „ " Apostrophes ‘ ’ ´ ' Dashes – — ― - Ligatures ﬁ ﬂ f Artifacts \u00ad \ _ Space

docs.title: Step 2: Taint Detection (The Gatekeeper)
docs.text:
As characters are read into the buffer, they are checked against the Strict Whitelist (ASCII 32-126).

  • Valid Char: Added to buffer.
  • Invalid Char (e.g., é, ñ, α): The current buffer is marked as TAINTED. The processor continues reading until the next separator (Space/Newline) to clear the bad token, but no stats are recorded for that token.
  • Effect: Words like naïve, façade, or garbage binary strings are completely dropped. The N-gram context is reset.

docs.title: Step 3: Tokenization Strategy
docs.text:
Once a valid (untainted) buffer is flushed (by space or punctuation), it undergoes structural processing:

  1. Double Dash Expansion: The sequence -- is explicitly treated as a separator.
  2. Input: today--actually
  3. Output: today, actually
  4. Multi-Hyphen Splitting: Words containing more than one hyphen are split into their constituent parts.
  5. Input: please-don't-shoot
  6. Output: please, don't, shoot
  7. Rationale: Prevents "sentence-words" from creating unique, statistically irrelevant tokens.
  8. Single Hyphens: Preserved (e.g., well-known).

docs.title: Step 4: Linguistic Validation
docs.text:
Before a token is accepted into words.json or the N-gram tracker, it must pass strict linguistic checks:

Check Rule Rationale Structure Strict ASCII Alpha + ' + - Rejects numbers (1990) and mixed-symbol strings. Length 1 <= len <= 25 Rejects OCR buffer overflows. Vowel Check Must contain [aeiouy] Rejects acronyms/noise (mzzt, krrk). Consonant Cluster Max 6 consecutive consonants Rejects agglutinative foreign words (e.g., Turkish) that slipped through. Repetition No 3+ identical chars Rejects expressive typing (nooooo).

docs.title: 2.3 Validation Tests
docs.text: Automated Python scripts (tests/validate_*.py) are integrated into the build pipeline to ensure data integrity.

docs.title: Test Suite 1: Vocabulary Verification (validate_vocabulary.py)
docs.text:
• Method: Cross-references words.json against a standard English dictionary (words_alpha.txt).
  • Metric: Token Volume Coverage.
  • Threshold: > 90% of the total text volume must be recognized English words.
  • Current Status: ~96.6% Coverage (Remaining 3.4% are valid contractions like don't).

docs.title: Test Suite 2: Structural Integrity (validate_1grams.py)
docs.text:
• Category Distribution: Verifies 100% of output chars are within the whitelist categories.
  • Artifact Scan: Scans for zero-occurrence of forbidden chars (\, _, â, \t).
  • Entropy: Verifies Shannon Entropy is within English norms (3.5 - 5.5 bits/char).

docs.title: Test Suite 3: N-Grams (validate_ngrams.py)
docs.text:
• Space Compression: Verifies that the bigram (" ", " ") does not exist.
  • Linguistic Consistency: Checks that the top 20 bigrams and trigrams align with standard English (e.g., "th", "he", "the", "and").

docs.title: 2.4 Weaknesses, Gaps, and Assumptions
docs.text: While en_std provides a robust baseline for prose typing, the following limitations apply:

docs.title: Domain Bias (Fiction)
docs.text:
• Dialogue Heavy: The corpus is dominated by fiction. Quotation marks and dialogue tags are over-represented.
  • Vocabulary: Technical, scientific, and legal vocabulary is under-represented.

docs.title: Strictness Trade-offs
docs.text:
• Loan Words: Common loan words with accents (café, jalapeño) are discarded entirely rather than normalized to (cafe, jalapeno). This is a trade-off for purity.
  • Numbers: Numeric tokens are excluded.
  • Modern Communication: The corpus does not reflect "internet slang," SMS-style abbreviations, or emoji usage.

docs.title: Layer Definitions
docs.text:
1. Drivers: Entry points that drive the application. They parse user input (CLI args, HTTP requests) and call the Application Layer.
  2. Adapters: Implementations of abstract interfaces for IO (Filesystem, Network, Database).
  3. Ports: The "Glue" layer. Defines the shape of the application (Runtime, Security protocols, DTOs) without binding to specific IO.
  4. Core: Pure business logic. Zero dependencies on the outer layers. Deterministic and testable.

docs.title: Design: KeyForge Adapter
docs.text: Responsibility: Anti-Corruption Layer (ACL) & Data Translation. Tier: 3 (The Adapter)

docs.title: 1. Purpose
docs.text:
The keyforge-adapter crate serves as the boundary between the external world (DTOs from keyforge-protocol) and the internal domain (Entities from keyforge-model).

It ensures that: 1. Validation: Raw data is validated before becoming a Domain Entity. 2. Decoupling: The Domain Layer never depends on the API Contract. 3. Versioning: API changes do not ripple into the Core logic.

docs.title: 2. Usage
docs.text:
use keyforge_adapter::conversion::TryIntoDomain;

let dto = JobRequestDto { ... };
let domain_entity: JobRequest = dto.try_into_domain()?;

docs.title: Design: KeyForge Agent
docs.text: Responsibility: Distributed computation (Worker). Tier: 3 (The Driver)

docs.title: 1. The Execution Loop
docs.text:
The Agent is a state machine that cycles between Polling, Computing, and Reporting.

stateDiagram-v2
    [*] --> Init
    Init --> Connect : Hardware Detected
    Connect --> Idle : WS Connected

    Idle --> Fetch : Job Signal Received
    Fetch --> Compute : Config Downloaded

    state Compute {
        [*] --> Prepare : Download Assets
        Prepare --> Optimize : Assets Ready
        Optimize --> Verify : Annealing Done
        Verify --> Sign : Deterministic Check Passed
    }

    Sign --> Submit : Signature Generated
    Submit --> Idle : Result Accepted

    Compute --> Idle : Error / Cancelled

docs.title: 2. Security Measures
docs.text:
• Deterministic Verification: The Agent re-runs the best layout through DeterministicScorer (Integer Math) to ensure the score is exact before signing.
  • Ed25519 Signing: Every result is signed with the node's private key. The Hive verifies this signature to prevent spoofing.

docs.title: Design: KeyForge Asset Manager
docs.text: Responsibility: Authoritative lifecycle management of system assets. Tier: 3 (The Daemon)

docs.title: 1. Core Philosophy: The Write Master
docs.text:
keyforge-assetmgr is the single source of truth for the state of assets in the distributed cluster. It is the only component permitted to write to the Asset keyspace in Valkey.

Unlike a simple loader, the Asset Manager is a long-running daemon that actively enforces consistency between the Source (Disk/Git) and the State (Valkey).

docs.title: Responsibilities
docs.text:
1. Hydration (Startup): Populates Valkey with the current state of the filesystem on boot.
  2. Synchronization (Hot Reload): Watches the filesystem for changes. When a developer or admin updates a JSON file, the manager immediately propagates the change to the cluster.
  3. Validation (The Gatekeeper): Before uploading any asset to Valkey, the Manager performs strict schema and logic validation (using keyforge-model). Invalid assets are rejected and logged; they never reach the serving layer.
  4. Garbage Collection: Detects removed files and purges their corresponding keys from Valkey to prevent cache bloat.

docs.title: 2. Architecture
docs.text:
graph TD
    Disk[(Filesystem)] <--> Watcher[FSEvent Watcher]
    Watcher --> Validator[Domain Validator]
    Validator -- Valid --> Serializer[Compression Engine]
    Serializer --> Writer[Valkey Writer]
    Writer --> Valkey[(Coordination Layer)]

    Validator -- Invalid --> Logger[Error Log]

docs.title: 3. Data Flow (The Write Loop)
docs.text:
sequenceDiagram
    participant Dev as Developer
    participant Disk as Local Volume
    participant Mgr as AssetMgr
    participant Valkey

    Dev->>Disk: Edit "weights/cost.json"

    Note over Mgr: File Watcher Event
    Mgr->>Disk: Read Content

    Mgr->>Mgr: Validate (Schema Check)
    alt Invalid
        Mgr->>Dev: Log Error (Skip Upload)
    else Valid
        Mgr->>Mgr: Compress (Zstd)
        Mgr->>Mgr: Calc Hash (SHA256)

        Mgr->>Valkey: SET asset:blob:weights/cost.json <bytes>
        Mgr->>Valkey: HSET v4:manifest:weights/cost.json hash <hash>

        Mgr->>Valkey: PUBLISH asset_updates "weights/cost.json"
    end

docs.title: 4. Modes of Operation
docs.text:
• daemon (Default): Performs initial hydration and then enters a blocking loop to watch for file changes.
  • hydrate: Performs a one-time synchronization and exits (useful for CI/CD pipelines).
  • verify: Runs validation logic against the filesystem without connecting to Valkey (dry run).

docs.title: 5. Operational Invariants
docs.text:
• Write Exclusivity: No other service (Hive, Assets, CLI) writes to asset:blob:*.
  • Validity Guarantee: If a key exists in Valkey, it is guaranteed to be a valid, loadable asset.
  • Eventual Consistency: There is a non-zero latency between a disk write and a Valkey update, but the Manager ensures convergence.

docs.title: Design: KeyForge Assets
docs.text: Responsibility: High-performance serving of static system assets. Tier: 3 (The Driver)

docs.title: 1. Architecture: The Data Plane
docs.text: keyforge-assets is a stateless HTTP server designed to serve read-only content from the distributed coordination layer (Valkey). It relieves keyforge-hive (The Control Plane) from I/O heavy operations.

docs.title: Deployment Model
docs.text:
• Stateless: No local disk dependency. All data comes from Valkey.
  • Scalable: Can be replicated infinitely behind a Load Balancer.
  • Public: Read-only access does not require authentication (simplifies client logic, relies on Hash Verification for integrity).

docs.title: Design: KeyForge CLI
docs.text: Responsibility: Local development, asset management, and Agent orchestration. Tier: 3 (The Driver)

docs.title: 1. The Thin Client Architecture
docs.text: The CLI has been refactored into a "Thin Client" that delegates heavy computation to the keyforge-agent. This separation ensures a consistent execution environment for optimization jobs, whether run locally or on the remote Hive cluster.

docs.title: Responsibilities
docs.text:
1. Asset Management (Native):
  2. The CLI directly manages the local workspace (data/) using keyforge-infra.
  3. It handles downloading assets (fetch), initializing workspaces (init), and managing user identity (auth).

  4. Why? These are IO-bound operations that do not require the Physics Engine.

  5. Job Orchestration (Delegated):

  6. For CPU-intensive tasks (search, benchmark, validate), the CLI acts as a driver.
  7. It constructs a JobConfig from command-line arguments.
  8. It spawns a keyforge-agent subprocess in "One-Shot" mode (keyforge-agent run).
  9. It streams the agent's output to the console for real-time feedback.

The Runtime struct is the primary entry point for clients (CLI, GUI) that want to execute physics operations. It bundles the stateless ScoringEngine with the stateful SearchConfig and KeycodeRegistry.

docs.title: Design: KeyForge Core
docs.text: Responsibility: Pure orchestration and helper functions. Tier: 2 (The Glue)

docs.title: 1. Orchestration Layer
docs.text:
keyforge-core exists to prevent circular dependencies between physics, evolution, and model. It provides high-level functions that coordinate these lower-level crates.

  • Constraint: NO IO allowed. This crate must compile to WASM.

docs.title: 2. Optimization Flow
docs.text:
sequenceDiagram
    participant Client
    participant Core
    participant Physics as ScoringEngine
    participant Evo as Evolution

    Client->>Core: optimize_with_engine(Engine, Config)

    Core->>Evo: evolve(Engine, Config)

    loop Annealing
        Evo->>Physics: score()
    end

    Evo-->>Core: OptimizationResult
    Core-->>Client: Result

docs.title: Design: KeyForge Evolution
docs.text: Responsibility: Stochastic optimization (Simulated Annealing). Tier: 1 (The Nucleus)

docs.title: 1. The Annealing Loop
docs.text:
The Optimizer drives the search for the global minimum.

sequenceDiagram
    participant Opt as Optimizer
    participant State as SearchState
    participant Mut as MutationOperator
    participant Eng as ScoringEngine

    Opt->>State: new(InitialLayout, Temp)

    loop Steps
        Mut->>Eng: Propose Swap(A, B)
        Eng-->>Mut: Delta (Score Change)

        alt Delta < 0 (Improvement)
            Opt->>State: Accept
        else Delta > 0 (Degradation)
            Opt->>State: Check Temperature Probability
            alt Random < P(Delta, Temp)
                Opt->>State: Accept
            else
                Opt->>State: Reject
            end
        end

        Opt->>State: Cool Down (Temp * 0.99)

        opt Patience Exceeded
            Opt->>State: Reheat (Temp = Start * Factor)
        end
    end

docs.title: 2. Strategies
docs.text:
• Cooling: Exponential decay.
  • Mutation: GroupMutation (swaps two keys within the unlocked set).
  • Reheating: If the score hasn't improved for N steps, the temperature is spiked to escape local minima.

    Logic --> Model
    Logic --> State
    State --> DB

docs.title: 2. The Worker Protocol (WebSocket)
docs.text:
Hive manages the Work distribution, not the Data distribution.

sequenceDiagram

    participant Hive
    participant Queue
    participant Assets as AssetServer

    Agent->>Hive: Connect (WS /ws?node_id=X)
    Hive-->>Agent: 101 Switching Protocols
